name: Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis
summary: Serotonin (5-HT) is a hormone and neurotransmitter used for regulatory purposes in animal CNS. In the human brain, serotonin is involved in many physiological functions such as sleep, pain, mood and is the precursor to melatonin, a hormone produced in the pineal gland.

reactions.name: Tryptophan is hydroxylated
reactions.summary: The first and rate limiting step in serotonin (5-HT) biosynthesis is catalyzed by tryptophan hydroxylase. The enzyme requires iron(II), tetrahydrobiopterin, and dioxygen cofactors for the hydroxylation of L-tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan. Tryptophan hydroxylase belongs to a small family of monooxygenases that utilize tetrahydrobiopterins. Other members are phenylalanine hydroxylase and tyrosine hydroxylase (Fitzpatrick, PF, 1999; Walther et al, 2003).

reactions.name: Decarboxylation of 5-hydroxytryptophan forms serotonin
reactions.summary: Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) catalyzes the decarboxylation of both dopa and 5-hydroxytryptophan to dopamine and serotonin, respectively. AADC functions as a homodimer, utilizing pyridoxal phosphate as a cofactor.
catalysts: aromatic-L-amino-acid decarboxylase activity of DDC dimer [cytosol]

reactions.name: N-acetylation of serotonin
reactions.summary: Serotonin N-acetyltransferase (AANAT) catalyzes the N-acetylation of serotonin to form N-acetylserotonin. AANAT utilizes acetyl-CoA as the donor of the acetyl group.

reactions.name: Methylation of N-acetyl-5-HT to form melatonin
reactions.summary: Hydroxyindole-O-methyltransferase (HIOMT) catalyzes the last step in the synthesis of melatonin. Melatonin is synthesized and released by the pineal gland and is thought to control circadian rhythms. HIOMT has 3 isoforms and utilizes S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) as the methyl donor in the conversion of N-acetyl-5HT to melatonin.
